problem.text: Agent memory keeps facts that later change; old and new versions both stay retrievable.

failure.text: The agent can't tell which value is current, and a late-arriving old record can look like the newest truth.

product.text: Named states with one current value, full history and sources; late records go into history; genuine disagreement is exposed, not guessed.

proof.text: 0.9.1 on PyPI; acceptance tests on three backends; a live explorer drawn from the product's own answers.

boundary.text: You name the key; no extraction from free text; one value per key; Python and CLI only for states.

experiment.hook: The rules we ended up with for late-arriving and conflicting values
experiment.channel: GitHub: three open issues that ask for exactly this (jcode #1106, fraise #390, kai #1702)

why_channel.reason: These maintainers wrote down this exact problem in the last six weeks, in their own repos
On HN the space is crowded with competing launches, so a Show HN would read as one more memory library

experiment.cta: How are you planning to order a value that arrives late but describes the past?
experiment.hypothesis: Maintainers designing validity/supersession right now will engage with concrete ordering rules (validity time vs arrival, weaker-later = conflict) more than with a library pitch; replies will show whether they'd adopt a state layer or only borrow the design.
experiment.message:
I maintain TypedMem, a small memory library, and hit exactly this. Sharing the rules we ended up with in case they're useful, whether or not you use the library:

1. Order values by when they became true (valid_from), not when they arrived. A late record describing the past goes into history; it doesn't replace the current value.
2. A later value from a weaker source doesn't silently win. It opens a conflict, and get() refuses to pick until stronger or later evidence settles it.
3. Nothing is deleted: every value keeps its window and its source.

Design note with the edge cases: https://github.com/lyr-ai/typedmem/blob/main/design/0002-changing-facts.md

One question: how are you planning to handle a value that arrives late but describes the past?
